evidence.note: No eval, no TODO/FIXME markers, no truncated chunks (all part 1/1), and each new lib file has a corresponding test file in this shard or shard-0/2.

findings.note: templates/mutation-incremental/lib/nodever.mjs:5-16: nodeVersionWarning stops at the first of .nvmrc/.node-version that exists and returns null immediately if that file's contents are a non-numeric alias (e.g. 'lts/*'), even when the other file exists and pins a numeric version. This matches the literal spec wording ('first of .nvmrc and .node-version that exists ... Aliases are skipped') so it is not a contract violation, just a corner case worth a comment; not a credible normal-usage failure since aliasing both files is unusual.

mutationtemplate_test.go:100-108: per-file coverage check greps the Node coverage report by filename with a word-boundary regex and counts '100.00' occurrences (>=3) on the matched line to assert 100% lines/branches/functions. This is coupled to Node's --test-coverage table formatting; if Node changes the report layout the assertion could false-negative/positive silently. Advisory only — it is a test-harness fragility, not a broken happy path in the reviewed code, and the suite reportedly runs green today (142/142 at 100% coverage).
